climate_pressure: Higher temperatures and warming-enhanced evaporative demand during multi-year drought.
documented_impact: More severe agricultural drought and water stress.
fcv_mediator: Irrigation dependence, livelihood losses, high input costs and limited alternatives.
possible_consequence: Where household buffers are weak, these pressures could increase distress mobility or socioeconomic grievances; violence is not demonstrated.
geographies: strongest livelihood relevance in irrigated agricultural areas
uncertainty: No national causal estimate links drought exposure to migration or grievances.
compact_statement: Warming-enhanced drought can worsen irrigation stress, but household and FCV consequences depend heavily on water governance and economic alternatives. (World Weather Attribution)

documented_impact: Reduced water availability and perceived worsening of water insecurity.
fcv_mediator: Allocation disputes, upstream/downstream differences, perceived injustice and competing sectoral claims.
possible_consequence: Local and regional water disputes may intensify when water insecurity and perception gaps are not managed.
alternative_explanations: agricultural policy and historical claims to water
uncertainty: Survey-based perception evidence cannot establish a unique climate causal effect.
resilience_factors: Social-learning platforms and conflict-sensitive stakeholder dialogue recommended by the study
compact_statement: In ZayandehRud, climate-related water stress is documented as one factor interacting with allocation and perceived injustice in local disputes - not as a stand-alone conflict cause. (Directory of Open Access Journals)

documented_impact: Reduced recharge and increased groundwater depletion during dry conditions.
fcv_mediator: Unsustainable withdrawals and governance of access to groundwater.
possible_consequence: Persistently depleted aquifers could deepen livelihood insecurity and competition among water users.
uncertainty: National groundwater evidence does not itself measure conflict outcomes.
compact_statement: Drought can accelerate groundwater depletion, but extensive human withdrawal is the dominant documented depletion driver; FCV risk would therefore be mediated by access and governance rather than climate alone. (Nature)

documented_impact: Need for finance, technology and institutional capacity.
fcv_mediator: Sanctions and restrictions on finance, technology and international cooperation.
possible_consequence: Adaptation planning or implementation may be slower, more expensive or narrower than otherwise possible.
uncertainty: The INDC is a government position and does not quantify sanctions' marginal adaptation effect.
compact_statement: Iran's own climate policy identifies sanctions and external restrictions as adaptation-capacity constraints, but the scale of their effect remains unevaluated. (Asia Pacific Energy Policy)

documented_impact: Stress on economic activity and infrastructure.
fcv_mediator: Conflict-related damage, sanctions, trade disruption, weak investment and import constraints.
possible_consequence: These conditions may reduce capacity to maintain, finance or upgrade water, energy and other climate-sensitive infrastructure.
uncertainty: No source in the verified set directly estimates lost adaptation investment.
resilience_factors: Institutional delivery arrangements insulated from direct financing channels
such as the World Bank/WHO COVID project model
compact_statement: Current FCV and economic disruption can plausibly narrow infrastructure-resilience capacity, although quantitative adaptation losses are unmeasured. (World Bank)

documented_impact: Pressure on wetlands and dependent livelihoods.
fcv_mediator: Competing water use, weak inter-organizational collaboration and livelihood dependence.
possible_consequence: Degradation could increase livelihood stress; participatory and integrated basin management may reduce such risk.
uncertainty: Programme reporting cannot establish counterfactual effectiveness.
compact_statement: Participatory wetland management provides a plausible resilience mechanism, but independent evidence of durable conflict- or vulnerability-reduction effects is missing. (UNDP)

fcv_mediator: Inflation, income pressure, food-market conditions and unequal household buffers.
possible_consequence: Combined pressures could raise grievances or lower coping capacity, especially among poorer households.
uncertainty: No verified study demonstrates a complete climate -> poverty -> grievance causal chain nationally.
compact_statement: Climate stress can add to household economic pressure, but sanctions, prices and conflict remain independent and potentially dominant explanations. (World Bank)

documented_impact: Need for more efficient production and basin coordination.
fcv_mediator: Institutional fragmentation and competing user interests.
possible_consequence: Multi-stakeholder institutions and livelihood alternatives may reduce vulnerability and provide channels for managing distributional tensions.
alternative_explanations: Programme participation may be uneven and gains may not persist after funding
uncertainty: No verified independent evaluation demonstrates peace outcomes.
compact_statement: Iran has observable institutional and community adaptation assets, but their contribution to durable peace or FCV reduction has not been independently demonstrated. (FAOHome)
